EDIT the attached front left car reference as the base image.

COMPOSITION PRIORITY: a very wide environmental tracking photograph with a small complete vehicle and generous overscan on ALL FOUR sides. The car occupies only 30–36% of the full image width. Preserve natural car proportions; never stretch the car to meet a height target. Center the complete car near x=50%, y=40%. Keep the bottoms of both tires above 53% of image height and leave the lower 40% uninterrupted for typography and branding. Pull the camera substantially farther away and extend the actual scene above, below, ahead of and behind the vehicle. Keep at least 25% of image width as environmental clearance ahead of the front bumper and behind the rear bumper where the selected text layout permits. Do not use a close-up hero shot, crop a bumper or tire, or enlarge the vehicle to fill unused space. The image must remain usable when cropped to 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9 and 1.91:1: leave continuous low-detail road and surroundings, not blank borders, letterboxing or artificially blurred padding. For a horizontal crop retain meaningful space above the roof and below the tires; for a narrow vertical crop retain both bumpers and side clearance. These are alternative crop options; preserve the selected typography zone in the requested output, with the full vehicle outside it. Architecture fills the upper background with almost no sky (0–5%). Surroundings dominate the image. Use the attached reference only for vehicle geometry, viewpoint and livery, never its tight crop or subject scale. Output aspect ratio 4:5.

This is an image-editing/background-replacement task, not a request to generate or redraw a new car from scratch. Use the original vehicle cutout wherever possible, compositing it into a photorealistic urban campaign photograph. Protect the car body and branding; replace or extend the surroundings, then integrate road contact shadows, lighting and panning effects around the original vehicle. If your tool supports masks, mask the surroundings for replacement while protecting the vehicle. Do not claim that a generative edit guarantees pixel-identical preservation; for exact branding, retain/composite the original car pixels rather than repainting the livery. Preserve the exact white sedan model, body proportions, wheels, grille, lights, windows, and WB Taxi livery from the reference, including the magenta/violet panel arrangement, door wordmark and number 260. Do not mirror, redesign or replace the car.

Windows and cabin: keep all windows fully closed. Use realistic dark reflective glazing, natural reflections of the surrounding architecture and sky, and a deeply shadowed cabin so no face is identifiable through the windshield or side windows. Preserve window transparency cues, glass edges and believable reflections; do not paint flat opaque black panels over the glass. If an occupant is visible at all, show only an indistinct silhouette behind the reflections, with no discernible eyes, mouth or facial features. Do not invent a visible driver portrait, open the window, brighten the cabin or expose a distorted face. Apply this to every angle, including front three-quarter views. Preserve the reference vehicle silhouette, mirrors and window geometry.

Omit the blank white front license plate and its mounting bracket: continue the grille pattern naturally behind it. Do not add any blank white number plates or placeholder rectangles at the front or rear.

Camera: a distant environment-led tracking shot from around door-handle height, with a level camera and natural 35–50 mm perspective; no upward-looking wide-angle hero perspective. Road geometry: the car is traveling LEFT, parallel to the curb and long lane boundaries. Show a side-on straight carriageway, with lane markings running predominantly left-to-right along the car longitudinal axis; no lanes crossing diagonally toward the camera, no crosswalk, no wrong-way traffic geometry. Road panning streaks follow the same lateral travel axis, never fan radially outward from the car. For the closest match choose the front-left three-quarter car reference, with the nose pointing left; preserve the selected reference angle and vehicle geometry. Follow the car scale and anchor in COMPOSITION PRIORITY; extend road and architecture on every side, respecting the selected layout safe area. Selected vehicle view: front-left three-quarter view, matching the reference viewpoint. Use the low, wide camera treatment described above. Show the entire vehicle, both bumpers and wheels, with breathing room around it.

Scene: a broad urban avenue beside one monumental modern facade, with tall pale stone piers, broad glass bays and a deep recessed dark ground floor. Frame architecture behind the car as indistinct broad masses, with every pier and glass bay heavily swept into horizontal tracking streaks; no crisp stone joints, sharp window mullions or clearly readable facade grid; show very little sky and no distant skyline, trees or street clutter. No trees, foliage, bushes or greenery anywhere, including reflections; no clouds. The selected street scene determines the architecture: do not replace walls, underpasses or open-road surroundings with a row of modern apartment buildings. If buildings are present, use just one or two broad, simple facade masses with large neutral surfaces. Suppress small windows, repetitive sharp facade grids, ornamental details, sharp distant skylines, street furniture and clusters of poles. Buildings are atmospheric color and light bands rather than an architectural subject. No crowds, prominent advertising, busy signage, traffic clutter or foreground obstructions.

Motion and light: the camera tracks the moving car at matching speed in a realistic panning shot. Keep the original car body and branding sharp and unchanged; show clearly visible rotational motion blur in the wheels and strong, long, coherent horizontal panning streaks across BOTH the building facades and road. Background windows, facade edges and road markings must visibly stretch into soft directional bands at normal viewing size. Gentle shallow depth of field or a slightly blurred road alone is not enough: the architecture must lose fine detail through motion. Aim for a slow-shutter tracking photograph, approximately 1/15–1/30 second, with the car tracked sharply. Keep the bodywork, WB Taxi wordmark, number 260 and every magenta/violet livery boundary tack sharp: no blur, smearing, warped letters, redrawn logos or altered graphic details on the car. Protect the original branded body pixels; apply motion blur only to separate background/road and wheel regions. If the tool cannot preserve the logo pixels exactly, retain the original car as a composited layer rather than regenerating its branding. warm low-angle sunset sunlight from the side, long realistic tire shadows and golden reflections on the body, with soft amber light on simple facades and a clear cloudless sky. Keep white paint believable and magenta/violet branding accurate; no heavy orange grading, artificial colored lighting or night scene. warm cream and champagne highlights on the architecture, deep desaturated petrol-green and charcoal shadows, and predominantly dark charcoal/petrol-green asphalt with only narrow restrained golden highlights near the tires. Finish with subtle fine 35 mm color-negative film grain: gently visible at full resolution in midtones and shadows, restrained in highlights. No coarse digital noise, heavy vintage filter, scratches, dust, halation, faded blacks or artificial sharpening. Follow the selected scene palette and structure; do not copy the warm office-building background or golden grading of another campaign image. Realistic tire contact and road shadow; no floating car, distorted geometry, radial zoom blur, speed-line graphics or blur across the branded bodywork.
